Description: The R&D system should consist of independent modules that can be added, removed, or expanded without breaking the core game.
Reason / Goal: Allow different complexity levels and future expansion.

Description: Technologies, effects, prerequisites, categories, and relationships should exist as structured data rather than being hardcoded into visualisations or scripts.
Reason / Goal: Enable multiple outputs and tools from the same underlying data.

Description: The base data file should contain the authoritative definitions of technologies and relevant system data.
Reason / Goal: Prevent inconsistencies between documentation, code, and visualisations.

Description: Research should create meaningful strategic planning rather than relying purely on random technology selection.
Reason / Goal: Allow players to pursue technological strategies and make informed commitments.

Description: Research capacity should compete with other economic uses of IPCs.
Reason / Goal: Create genuine strategic trade-offs.

Description: Technologies should be inspired by WWII developments but adapted where necessary for gameplay.
Reason / Goal: Preserve the Axis & Allies feel while allowing alternate histories.

Description: Historical accuracy may be modified when necessary for gameplay balance.
Reason / Goal: Prevent realism from creating dominant or unfun mechanics.

Description: Advanced technologies require appropriate preceding technologies or other defined prerequisites.
Reason / Goal: Create meaningful technological progression and prevent arbitrary jumps.

Description: Powerful capabilities should normally be reached through discrete, meaningful intermediate technologies rather than through a single leap or arbitrary multi-stage payment process for one technology.
Reason / Goal: Make technological development progressive while preserving the discrete nature of technologies.

Description: Technology branches should provide useful choices, meaningful capabilities, or lead toward meaningful developments; an item may legitimately be the endpoint of a technological dependency trail.
Reason / Goal: Prevent genuinely unproductive research paths without requiring every technology to unlock another technology.

Description: Where appropriate, important capabilities may be reachable through different prerequisite paths.
Reason / Goal: Support strategic diversity and alternate approaches.

Description: Alternatives within a dependency group are OR requirements, while separate dependency groups are combined as AND requirements.
Reason / Goal: Support nuanced technological dependencies while keeping their semantics explicit and machine-readable.

Description: The technology tree should remain readable and navigable as it expands.
Reason / Goal: Preserve usability for human players.

Description: The meaning, rules, and relationships of the technology system should be independent of how they are visually displayed.
Reason / Goal: Permit multiple visualisation and interface formats without changing the underlying system.

Description: The data structure should support an eventual interactive technology-tree interface, including filtering, highlighting, dependency exploration, module selection, and research-state tracking.
Reason / Goal: Allow the system to evolve into interactive tools without restructuring its fundamental data.

Description: Technologies and technological paths should reflect national strengths, weaknesses, or specialisation where appropriate.
Reason / Goal: Preserve Axis & Allies national identity and flavour.

Description: The basic R&D system should remain playable while optional modules can add additional depth.
Reason / Goal: Allow groups to choose their desired complexity.

Description: Mechanics should create meaningful strategic decisions rather than excessive bookkeeping or repetitive administration.
Reason / Goal: Keep the system practical during an actual game.

Description: The system should be structured so calculations, validation, visualisations, and repetitive tasks can eventually be automated.
Reason / Goal: Reduce manual maintenance and improve reliability.

Description: Technologies and other data objects should have stable IDs independent of displayed names.
Reason / Goal: Support renaming, localisation, software integration, and long-term data maintenance.

Description: Every research attempt costs exactly 1 Research Point (RP), independent of technology tier, power, or complexity.
Reason / Goal: Keep the research economy simple and make technological difficulty emerge primarily from eligibility and progression rather than variable RP prices.

Description: One RP represents one opportunity to attempt acquisition of one eligible technology. RP are not accumulated progress toward a technology.
Reason / Goal: Avoid progress-bar bookkeeping and preserve the discrete nature of technologies.

Principle: RP are the core research resource
Description: Research Points are the established resource used to conduct research attempts.
Reason / Goal: Provide a dedicated research-capacity economy separate from direct technology purchasing.

Description: The current baseline conversion is 5 IPC → 1 RP.
Reason / Goal: Establish a simple economic relationship between general spending and research capacity while retaining a parameter that can be balanced.

Description: Unspent RP carry over between turns.
Reason / Goal: Allow players to accumulate research capacity and choose when to commit it.

Description: A player's available or committed RP are public information, while the technology targeted by a research attempt remains secret until resolution.
Reason / Goal: Create strategic information without revealing exact technological intentions.

Description: RP are assigned to research attempts at the beginning of the player's turn, alongside normal unit purchases.
Reason / Goal: Establish a clear commitment point and prevent mid-turn reactionary research.

Description: When an RP is assigned, the player secretly selects an eligible technology as its research target.
Reason / Goal: Preserve uncertainty and allow hidden technological intentions.

Description: Research eligibility is evaluated at the beginning of the turn and remains fixed for that turn's assignments.
Reason / Goal: Prevent newly acquired technologies from changing the validity of already-committed research.

Description: Technologies acquired during the current turn cannot make additional technologies eligible for that turn's already-assigned research attempts.
Reason / Goal: Ensure multiple RP increase research breadth without bypassing technological depth.

Description: A player may assign multiple RP to different eligible technologies during the same turn.
Reason / Goal: Allow research capacity to increase breadth without imposing an arbitrary one-technology-per-turn restriction.

Description: Research attempts are resolved during the deployment phase, when their targets are revealed.
Reason / Goal: Separate research commitment from resolution and integrate research naturally into the turn sequence.

Description: A research roll of 1 fails; the RP is lost and the targeted technology remains undisclosed.
Reason / Goal: Provide a simple failure state while preserving research secrecy.

Description: A research roll of 2–5 acquires the targeted technology and consumes the RP.
Reason / Goal: Establish the normal research outcome.

Description: A research roll of 6 acquires the targeted technology while retaining the RP for the following round.
Reason / Goal: Provide an exceptional outcome that increases future research capacity without creating same-turn acceleration.

Description: An RP retained through a breakthrough becomes available for the following round and cannot immediately fund another attempt during the current turn.
Reason / Goal: Prevent breakthrough results from creating uncontrolled same-turn research acceleration.

Description: Failure does not reveal which technology was targeted.
Reason / Goal: Make failed research strategically meaningful without giving opponents free information.

Principle: Tree controls eligibility; economy controls capacity
Description: The technology tree determines what a player is eligible to research, while the RP economy determines how many research attempts the player can make.
Reason / Goal: Clearly separate technological progression from research capacity.

Description: Additional RP allow additional simultaneous attempts among technologies eligible at the start of the turn, but do not bypass prerequisite depth.
Reason / Goal: Prevent the research economy from undermining the technology tree.

Principle: Tree and economy divide pacing responsibilities
Description: The technology tree provides much of the pacing through prerequisites and technological depth; the research economy controls the rate at which eligible opportunities can be attempted.
Reason / Goal: Avoid relying on variable technology prices or artificial per-turn limits as the primary pacing mechanism.

Description: Additional sources or bonuses to RP—such as objectives, universities, captured research assets, espionage, etc.—should be treated as separate future modules rather than assumed core rules.
Reason / Goal: Allow the research economy to expand without destabilising its core mechanism.

Description: Resources required, produced, consumed, or used as prerequisites—such as Aluminium, Steel, Oil, Vril, Heavy Water, and Uranium—are represented explicitly as resources rather than classified as technologies.
Reason / Goal: Preserve the semantic distinction between things that are researched and things that support, enable, or constrain technological development.

Description: Whether an item is optional is represented independently from its Category, Module, Path, or other classification.
Reason / Goal: Prevent a single classification field from carrying multiple unrelated meanings and allow optional items to participate normally in dependency and path structures.

Description: Path labels identify items that participate in particular technological or dependency routes. An item may belong to multiple paths. Paths do not inherently represent mutually exclusive research programmes selected by the player.
Reason / Goal: Support strategic and visual analysis without artificially restricting items to a single research direction.

Principle: One canonical graph, multiple derived views
Description: The complete technology graph should be constructed once from canonical data. Different visualisations, filters, highlights, and selections should be derived through view logic rather than separate copies or altered versions of the underlying technology structure.
Reason / Goal: Ensure consistency between FULL and specialised views while allowing flexible presentation and analysis.

Description: The R&D system's core rules should apply consistently to both Global 1940 and Global 1940 Halifax. For Halifax purposes, the UK is treated as a single economy, while ANZAC represents Canada, South Africa, and the normal ANZAC forces/economy collectively.
Reason / Goal: Ensure the R&D system remains compatible across both game configurations without requiring fundamentally different rulesets.

Description: Strategic resources may function as abstract national resources alongside IPCs without requiring physical transportation across the map. Their production may be geographically located and strategically contested while their use remains nationally accessible.
Reason / Goal: Preserve strategic competition over resources without introducing supply-line, tanker, or transport bookkeeping.

Description: Resource production should be connected to meaningful geographical locations where territorial control can influence strategic resource availability.
Reason / Goal: Make the map and territorial conquest economically and strategically significant.

Description: Not all available resources need be automatically productive. Resource production may require infrastructure or economic investment, creating choices between immediate military expenditure and longer-term development.
Reason / Goal: Create meaningful economic and developmental decisions.

Principle: Core and technologically enhanced infrastructure are distinct
Description: Basic resource infrastructure should remain conceptually distinct from infrastructure or capabilities enabled or improved by technological development. Basic resource systems should not require R&D to function, while R&D may expand or improve them.
Reason / Goal: Allow technology to interact with and deepen a resource system without making the basic module dependent on research.

Principle: Optional resource modules may have internal progression
Description: A resource module may contain its own progression from geographical resources through infrastructure and production to operational use and technological enhancement.
Reason / Goal: Allow resource systems to create meaningful strategic depth rather than functioning solely as passive modifiers.

Description: Facilities are physical game pieces placed on the map and subject to the normal territorial and physical interactions of the game.
Reason / Goal: Integrate infrastructure directly into the strategic map and economy.

Description: A facility represents a physical installation or infrastructure capability, while a technology represents researched knowledge/capability.
Reason / Goal: Maintain a clear semantic distinction between what is researched and what is built.

Description: A technology may unlock the ability to build or purchase a facility or base.
Reason / Goal: Allow technological development to produce tangible strategic infrastructure.

Principle: Research Centres are the facility prerequisite exception
Description: Research Centres may be required for research eligibility. Other facility/base types do not themselves function as technology prerequisites.
Reason / Goal: Keep technological dependencies centred on technologies while allowing research infrastructure to gate research.

Principle: Facility unlocks do not become technology dependencies
Description: When a technology unlocks a facility, subsequent technological development normally depends on the unlocking technology rather than possession of the physical facility.
Reason / Goal: Prevent physical infrastructure ownership from unnecessarily becoming part of the technology graph.

Description: Facilities can have states such as operational, damaged, captured, or otherwise disabled according to their individual rules.
Reason / Goal: Make infrastructure interact meaningfully with warfare and territorial control.

Description: A facility's gameplay effect is defined by its own rules rather than by a universal assumption about what all facilities do.
Reason / Goal: Allow research centres, production facilities, resource facilities, and other infrastructure to have different roles.

Description: Facility/base status and specialised classifications such as `RCENTER` are represented explicitly in the research data.
Reason / Goal: Allow the software and visualisations to distinguish physical infrastructure from ordinary technologies.

Principle: Research Centre capabilities may include RP generation
Description: A Research Centre may provide research capacity or other research-related effects when explicitly defined by its rules.
Reason / Goal: Allow universities and other research infrastructure to contribute to the research economy without making RP generation an inherent property of every facility.

Description: Technologies can unlock the ability to build or purchase facilities, while the facilities themselves have individually determined costs. Facility costs can therefore differentiate the practical impact of technologies with different levels of capability.
Reason / Goal: Provide an additional balancing lever between technological access and actual deployment of the resulting capability.
